x: They also did well in the short sprints with Lewis scoring a double and our only placed man in these events was Les Christmas, third in the 220.
Lewis, now demobbed from the Forces, ran well and should be a help to our junior teams, and Len. Bishop, also back again in civvy street, was another welcome visitor.

However, he won his heat O.K., and in the final was placed 3rd to Grieve of S.L.H. and Lewis of Walton. The 880 yards saw Bob Taylor continue his good form by winning the race in 1 min. 57.3 secs. which equalled last year's time.

Lewis(Woodford) and Pape (Portsmouth) were in contrast here and it was surprising to see Pape go away quite easily. Dave Baulch, usually on a later stage, was having a change of scenery this year but as he was surrounded by Internationals he not surprisingly had to relinquish two vital places.
After a mile he was still amongst the leaders and a little later began to force the pace on Lewis(Woodford), Stacey(T.V.H.) and Cornell(Chelmsford).
Ron Shipley, after a bad spell at half way recovered well and only just failed to catch Chapman and Lewis of Woodford, who were 4th and 5th.
He was forced to give way to Collins of Shaftesbury who went from 6th to 2nd and Lewis of Woodford (10th to 4th), but was able to displace Blackheath.
Lewis of Woodford, running at his best, and Perkins of Ilford were making great progress from behind and up the long slope past Croydon Airport forced Ron to concede further places.
Such names as Ovett, Moorcroft, Pirie, Cram, Lewis, Hutchings and Bedford to mention only a few bear witness to the benefits of winter competition.

Carl Lewis crazy ..." The Brits. were a little depressed after Backley and McKean made surprisingly early exits but the whole trip became worthwhile, just to be at the trackside for the 100 metres final.
SoEAA Champs. 60mH: 1, N.Owen 8.1(CBP), Neil shared the same time as second placer Lewis of Wolves - both were two metres clear of the rest.

There have been some superb world sprinters in the last decade – Burrell, Lewis, Fredericks, Christie, Bailey, etc. – and the current crop is tremendous – Ato Boldon, Maurice Greene – but none of them have run faster than the Belgrave boy at 19 years of age.
